# Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition

[Submitted on 28 Aug 2026]

# Title: Dynamic Alignment Compensation for Hallucination Mitigation in Large Vision-Language Models

Authors: Kairong Yu , Zixin Zhu , Le Yu , Hongwei Wang

View a PDF of the paper titled Dynamic Alignment Compensation for Hallucination Mitigation in Large Vision-Language Models, by Kairong Yu and 3 other authors

View PDF HTML (experimental)

> Abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) remain prone to hallucinations, producing responses that are irrelevant or inconsistent with the multimodal input. Existing mitigation methods mainly rely on external supervision, output calibration, or attention regulation, leaving the internal representation dynamics of autoregressive generation underexplored. We identify an inference-time failure mode in which cross-modal representations degrade across decoder layers and drift across generation steps, destabilizing token prediction and increasing hallucination risk. We propose Dynamic Alignment Compensation (DAC), a training-free inference-time method that detects representation divergence and selectively applies lightweight residual compensation. DAC combines Layer-wise Semantic Compensation to mitigate inter-layer degradation with Sequential Semantic Correction to constrain temporal drift. Experiments on nine hallucination-focused and general-purpose multimodal benchmarks across multiple LVLM backbones show that DAC consistently reduces hallucinations while maintaining strong overall performance.

Accepted by EMNLP2026 Findings

summaryZh: 针对大视觉语言模型（LVLMs）在生成过程中跨模态表征跨层退化和跨步骤漂移导致的幻觉问题，本文提出了动态对齐补偿（DAC）训练期外推理方法。DAC 通过结合层级语义补偿与序列语义 correction，选择性地应用轻量级残差补偿来检测并修正表征分歧。多项多模态基准测试表明，该方法在保持模型整体性能的同时，显著降低了幻觉率。
